correctness.rationale: All 3,003 row sets and 3,003 column sets are partitioned into 201 translation orbits (200 size 15, one size 3); independent translations multiply Fourier entries by invertible diagonal phases. For 40,401 orbit representative pairs, the complete 5x5 rank is computed by exact signed-permutation minor polynomials reduced modulo the irreducible cyclotomic polynomial Phi_15=X^8-X^7+X^5-X^4+X^3-X+1. The minor criterion proves each rank over C, with lower minor checks down to size 2. Weighted counts yield ranks 2:360, 3:24480, 4:880920, 5:8112249, totalling 9,018,009. An independent modular Gaussian elimination check at primes 31 and 61 achieves the exact rank as the maximum of the two lower bounds in all 40,401 cases. The rank-two coset construction analytically counts 360; its converse follows from the complete exact incidence scan. Rank one is analytically excluded using annihilating difference subgroups and 25>15.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural complete five-frequency sampling classification for squarefree C15, enumerating precisely how many observations lose zero, one, two, or three independent Fourier degrees. The 360 deepest losses admit a sharp coset-residue characterization and are not implied by an existing four-frequency rank table; the complete finite incidence matrix is reusable for testing Fourier recovery and uncertainty claims. The exact invariant is motivated by interpolation and rank-deficiency theory, not an arbitrary subfamily.
